dataset.name: amazon_sale_report
dataset.description: Line-item level Amazon.in order records for a clothing/apparel seller, covering orders placed between late March 2022 and June 2022. Each row is one SKU line within one order.
dataset.grain: One row = one order line (one SKU quantity within one Order ID). An Order ID can appear on multiple rows if it contains multiple SKUs.
dataset.primary_key: Order ID + SKU (not strictly unique alone; treat 'index' as the row id)

fields.name: index
fields.description: Row identifier, not a business key.

fields.name: Order ID
fields.description: Amazon order identifier. One order can span several rows (one per SKU/item).

fields.name: Date
fields.description: Order date.

fields.name: Status
fields.description: Detailed order/shipment status as reported by Amazon.

grouping_for_chatbot.description: When a user asks a broad question like 'how many orders were cancelled/delivered/returned', map to these buckets instead of exact string matches.

fields.name: Fulfilment
fields.description: Who fulfilled the order.

fields.name: Sales Channel
fields.note: Column name in the raw file has a trailing space: 'Sales Channel '.
fields.description: Platform the order came through.

fields.name: ship-service-level
fields.description: Shipping speed tier.

fields.name: Style
fields.description: Style/design code, shared across sizes and color variants of the same product design (e.g. all sizes of style JNE3781 are one design).

fields.name: SKU
fields.description: Stock keeping unit. Encodes style + color/variant + size, e.g. 'JNE3781-KR-XXXL' = style JNE3781, size XXXL.

fields.name: Category
fields.description: Product category/garment type.
fields.note: Values are case-sensitive as stored ('kurta' lowercase, others capitalized). Chatbot should match case-insensitively.

fields.name: Size
fields.description: Garment size.

fields.name: ASIN
fields.description: Amazon Standard Identification Number, the Amazon-wide product identifier.

fields.name: Courier Status
fields.description: Status from the courier/logistics side (distinct from order Status).
fields.null_meaning: No courier assigned yet or not applicable (common for Cancelled orders).

fields.name: Qty
fields.description: Units ordered on this line. 0 typically corresponds to Cancelled orders.

fields.name: currency
fields.description: Currency of Amount. Effectively always INR when present; null for orders with no amount (mostly cancelled).

fields.name: Amount
fields.description: Order line value in INR. Null for many cancelled orders.
fields.notes: Sum(Amount) is the standard 'revenue' metric, but see business_rules.revenue_definition before including/excluding cancelled orders.

fields.name: ship-city
fields.description: Buyer's shipping city (free text, ~8,955 distinct values, inconsistent casing).

fields.name: ship-state
fields.description: Buyer's shipping state. Messy/inconsistent: mixed case (e.g. 'Bihar' vs 'BIHAR' vs 'bihar'), abbreviations (e.g. 'RJ', 'PB', 'NL', 'AR'), misspellings ('Rajshthan', 'Rajsthan'), and old/alt names ('Orissa' -> Odisha, 'Pondicherry' -> Puducherry).
fields.instruction_for_chatbot: Before grouping or filtering by state, uppercase-trim the value and apply the normalization map so variants of the same state are combined.

fields.name: ship-postal-code
fields.description: Buyer's shipping postal/PIN code.

fields.name: ship-country
fields.description: Always 'IN' (India) when present.

fields.name: promotion-ids
fields.description: Raw list of promotion/discount identifiers applied to the order; null if no promotion applied. ~62% of rows have at least one promotion id.

fields.name: B2B
fields.description: Whether the order was business-to-business. Rare (~0.7% of rows).

fields.name: fulfilled-by
fields.description: Populated only for Merchant-fulfilled orders using Amazon's 'Easy Ship' program; null for Amazon-fulfilled orders.

fields.name: Unnamed: 22
fields.description: Empty/unused trailing column from the source export. Exclude from all analysis and from the chatbot's answerable fields.

business_rules.revenue_definition: Default 'revenue' or 'sales' metric = SUM(Amount) over rows where Status is NOT 'Cancelled' (cancelled orders mostly have Amount/currency null or a nominal placeholder value and don't represent real sales). If the user explicitly asks for gross/booked revenue including cancellations, sum Amount over all rows instead and state that cancellations are included.
business_rules.unit_sales_definition: 'Units sold' or 'quantity sold' = SUM(Qty). Qty is 0 for most cancelled rows, so this naturally excludes them; state this if asked.
business_rules.order_count_vs_line_count: Because one Order ID can have multiple SKU lines, COUNT(DISTINCT Order ID) = number of orders, while COUNT(*) or row count = number of order lines/items. Always clarify which one is being asked for ('how many orders' vs 'how many items').
business_rules.cancellation_rate: COUNT(DISTINCT Order ID WHERE Status = 'Cancelled') / COUNT(DISTINCT Order ID) overall.
business_rules.return_rate: COUNT(DISTINCT Order ID WHERE Status IN ('Shipped - Returned to Seller','Shipped - Returning to Seller')) / COUNT(DISTINCT Order ID WHERE Status LIKE 'Shipped%').
business_rules.average_order_value: SUM(Amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT Order ID), computed over non-cancelled orders unless stated otherwise.
business_rules.missing_amount_currency: Amount/currency are null on ~7,795 rows, overwhelmingly cancelled orders. Treat as 'no sale value', not zero, when averaging.
business_rules.state_field_quality: Always apply the ship-state normalization map (see fields.ship-state) before any state-level aggregation or 'top states' question, or results will double-count the same state under different spellings.
business_rules.date_scope: The dataset only covers ~3 months (Mar 31 - Jun 29, 2022). If a user asks about a period outside this range, say the data doesn't cover it rather than extrapolating.

revenue.label: Revenue
revenue.description: Total sales value excluding cancelled orders.

gross_revenue.label: Gross Revenue
gross_revenue.notes: Only use when user explicitly asks to include cancelled orders.

line_item_count.label: Line Item Count
line_item_count.description: Number of rows in the dataset.

cancellation_rate.label: Cancellation Rate
cancellation_rate.formula: COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN Status='Cancelled' THEN `Order ID` END) / COUNT(DISTINCT `Order ID`)

return_rate.label: Return Rate
return_rate.formula: COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN Status IN ('Shipped - Returned to Seller', 'Shipped - Returning to Seller') THEN `Order ID` END) / COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN Status LIKE 'Shipped%' THEN `Order ID` END)

promotion_penetration.label: Promotion Penetration
promotion_penetration.formula: COUNT(CASE WHEN `promotion-ids` IS NOT NULL AND `promotion-ids` <> 'Unknown' THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*)

b2b_share.label: B2B Share
b2b_share.formula: COUNT(CASE WHEN B2B = TRUE THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*)

fba_share.label: Fulfilled by Amazon Share
fba_share.formula: COUNT(CASE WHEN Fulfilment='Amazon' THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*)

derived_flags.is_returned: Status in ['Shipped - Returned to Seller', 'Shipped - Returning to Seller']

common_questions_to_query_map.user_asks: What was total revenue / sales in [month]?
common_questions_to_query_map.logic: Filter Date to month, filter Status != 'Cancelled', SUM(Amount).

common_questions_to_query_map.user_asks: What's the best-selling category / style / SKU?
common_questions_to_query_map.logic: GROUP BY Category (or Style/SKU), SUM(Qty) or SUM(Amount), ORDER BY desc, exclude Cancelled if measuring real sales.
Normalize ship-state first, then GROUP BY ship-state, SUM(Amount), exclude Cancelled.
Filter Category, GROUP BY Size, SUM(Qty).

common_questions_to_query_map.user_asks: What % of orders use Amazon fulfilment vs merchant?
common_questions_to_query_map.logic: COUNT(DISTINCT Order ID) GROUP BY Fulfilment, divide by total distinct orders.
SUM(Amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT Order ID) WHERE Status != 'Cancelled'.

common_questions_to_query_map.user_asks: How many orders had a promotion applied?
common_questions_to_query_map.logic: COUNT(DISTINCT Order ID) WHERE promotion-ids IS NOT NULL.

common_questions_to_query_map.user_asks: How many B2B orders were there?
common_questions_to_query_map.logic: COUNT(DISTINCT Order ID) WHERE B2B == True.

chatbot_response_guidelines.always_state_scope: When answering, mention the time window covered (Mar 31-Jun 29, 2022) if the user's question could imply a longer period.
chatbot_response_guidelines.clarify_orders_vs_lines: If ambiguous, default to 'orders' (distinct Order ID) for counts, and clarify Amount/Qty are summed at the line level.
chatbot_response_guidelines.clarify_cancelled_handling: When reporting revenue/sales figures, briefly note whether cancelled orders were excluded.
chatbot_response_guidelines.no_pii_beyond_dataset: Only ship-city/state/postal-code/country are available; no customer names, emails, or payment details exist in this dataset -- do not imply otherwise.
unanswerable_examples: Profit margin or cost data (not in dataset)
Customer identity/repeat-customer analysis (no customer ID field)
